chapter: The Vitaphone film and studio work
title: Making the Vitaphone film for Warner Bros. in 1927
summary: While at the Follies Theater, Byron Foy hired Spikes's band to make a Vitaphone short for Warner Bros., about 45 minutes with entertainers and dancers.

bands.name: Reb Spikes and His Majors and Minors Orchestra

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: In that...during...around that time that you made...you still haven't talked on the tape about that film you made at Warner Bros...or Vita...Vita...Vitaphone...Vitagraph?
Yeah, well, that was...it was called Vitaphone at first.
And you were appearing at The Follies Theater downtown.
With your band, and that's where...

Byron Foy came in and hired us to make the picture. Of the Foy Brothers. And we went out and made the picture for Warner Bros., and I showed you the letter, and he recommended the band very highly for Victor Record Company. And this was made...this picture was made before Al Jolson.
And it was a sound film, and as far as you know, it was the first sound film...
Of any consequences, you know. They had been making, I think, some before that. Little pictures...trying out, you know. This was a trial, too. But it was a...

Forty five or an hour or something like that-- around forty five... We played about eight or ten numbers, you know, for...at...in the entertainment, what a band could do...about a hour. We had five or six entertainers...and dancers...and three or four musical numbers.
